content: Gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM) diagnostic criteria and their global consensus have been evaluated, particularly focusing on the impact of GDM diagnosis. Pregnancies in which GDM was identified using the International Association of Diabetes and Pregnancy Study Groups (IADPSG) criteria, but not recognized by the traditional two-step method, exhibit health outcomes that are comparable to those diagnosed using the two-step criteria. This observation indicates that the one-step method may identify cases of GDM that are overlooked by the two-step method. Consequently, this could result in improved health management and potentially better clinical outcomes for both the mother and the fetus.
